# Image prompt system (Google Nano Banana, generated by hand)

Claude writes `05_prompts/prompts.json`. `prompts_tool.py` turns it into the copyable sheet `prompts.md`, the bulk list `all_prompts.txt` and `manifest.json`. **Claude writes only the subject-specific fields.** The tool adds the fixed style block, the green-screen instructions, the face rules and the negative list, so every prompt in every video stays consistent. Never hand-paste style text into the fields.

## World block (required)
Every prompts.json starts with `"world": "<place, year, who the people are, period clothing; no European/modern people, clothes or objects>"`. It is appended to every prompt. Image generators drift to European or modern people without it.

## Shape

```json
{
  "title": "He Paid To Feed His Killers 🤔",
  "characters": {
    "C1": {"name": "Old adviser", "kit": "A 65-year-old Ottoman court adviser, thin, long white beard, ... (identity kit: age, build, hair, facial hair + 3-4 costume items with TWO signature colours)"},
    "C2": {"name": "Sultan", "kit": "..."}
  },
  "scene_lines": {"S01": "narration of the shot, shown as the section heading"},
  "round1": [ {"id": "C1_REF", "kind": "ref", "character": "C1"} ],
  "round2": [ ... ]
}
```

## Kinds and fields

| kind | what it is | Claude fills | becomes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ref` | character reference, full body, front view, on green. **Round 1, made first** | `character` | cut-out, used as the `attach` reference for every pose |
| `char` | one pose of a character on green | `character`, `pose`, `view`, `framing`, `light`, `used_in`; `attach` is set automatically to `["C1_REF"]` (write it) | cut-out layer |
| `prop` | single object on green | `desc`, `view`, `light`, `used_in` | cut-out layer |
| `bg` | empty set, no people | `desc`, `camera`, `light`, `space` (where the floor / free area is), `used_in` | full-frame plate |
| `full` | finished frame (the default for most shots); `edit_of` + `change` for a second pose of an existing frame | `desc` (who does what, naming `C1_REF`…), `camera`, `light`, `attach` (refs + optional bg), `used_in` | full-frame plate with faces |
| `insert` | close-up plate: hands, documents, maps, objects on a table | `desc`, `camera`, `light`, `used_in` | full-frame plate |

Optional on any entry: `note` (shown next to the ID, e.g. "reuse for S14"), and `override` (full custom prompt text; avoid it).

## IDs (the user saves each image under its ID)
- Character references: `C1_REF`, `C2_REF` …
- Poses: `C1_P01`, `C1_P02` … (per character, in order of first use)
- Backgrounds: `BG_01` …
- Props: `P_01` … (or a readable `P_SACK`, `P_COIN`)
- Combined frames: `S07_FULL` (scene number of first use)
- Inserts: `S12_INS`
- Uppercase letters, digits and `_` only.

## Plan for animation (these rules beat everything above)
The target animates characters that **cut out cleanly**. Plan images so ours can too:
1. In **at least 60 % of shots, the protagonist** is on screen. In about **60 % of all shots, ONE character (or two)** stands on a **simple, uncluttered background**: open sky, starfield, plain wall, rooftop, a mountain of gold on a plain glow. Their whole outline is clear and nobody stands close behind them. These shots get split layers and full energy.
2. Give **2–3 poses (`edit_of`) to about 35–40 % of shots**. Poses are **theatrical and exaggerated**: head thrown back laughing, arms flung wide, pockets turned out, collapsing, pointing, shrugging. Not standing neutrally.
3. Frame characters **mid-shot to full-body** (50–70 % of frame height), not tight close-ups. The target's eyes are small in frame but clear on the face.
4. Crowds, bazaars and landscapes are short establishing shots (at most ~25 % of shots). **Never use the same image in two shots in a row; any image at most twice per video.**
5. Every project sets a **`look`** block (appended to every prompt): clean, vivid colours, clear air, no dust haze, bright clear skies, sharp outline against a simple background, theatrical body language. Plan at least 25 % cool, blue or night shots so the palette isn't all sepia.

## How to split a shot into images (the reference method)
The reference builds almost every shot from **one finished frame per pose**. The engine cuts the people out of it automatically (`split_layers.py`) and moves subject and background apart in 2.5D. So:

1. **Default: `full` plates.** One finished frame per shot, with the characters in the set, the right camera angle and lighting, attaching the character refs. This gives the best lighting and integration and the depth comes for free.
2. **Pose swaps = edit-mode images.** For the second pose of a shot, write an entry with `"edit_of": "<first image ID>"` and `"change": "<only what changes>"`. The tool writes a Nano Banana **EDIT** prompt that keeps place, framing and light identical. Never describe the second pose as a fresh scene, because fresh generations drift to new locations. Plan 1 second pose for about 35–40 % of shots.
3. **`prop` cut-outs** for anything that must fall, pop, slide or multiply (sacks, coins, map pins, bombs) and for small moving parts (a hand with a knife, a rowing boat).
4. **`bg` plates** only where props or cut-outs need an empty set to land on (the deck before the sacks fall).
5. **`char` cut-outs** only when one character must walk across or be reused on several backgrounds.
6. **`insert`** for hands-only close-ups, maps, letters and coins in a palm.

Example pair:
```json
{"id": "S06A_FULL", "kind": "full", "attach": ["PS_REF"], "used_in": ["S06"], "desc": "PS_REF stands straining, hugging a huge sack of silver ..."},
{"id": "S06B_FULL", "kind": "full", "edit_of": "S06A_FULL", "used_in": ["S06"], "change": "he has slumped down and now sits on the pile of sacks hugging one sack in his lap, looking up"}
```

## Writing good fields
- **kit**: copied word for word into every prompt of that character, so make it complete and fixed: age, build, skin, hair, facial hair, 3–4 costume items, two signature colours. Never change it mid-story.
- **pose**: a clear body action that shows the emotion, since the cartoon face is added later ("leaning back with arms crossed, chin up", "kneeling with hands clasped, pleading"). The face itself stays neutral, with eyes open and mouth closed. The tool adds that rule.
- **view**: front / three-quarter left / three-quarter right / profile (avoid profile for characters that need cartoon faces) / back view.
- **framing**: "full body" for LS/MLS; "from the knees up" or "waist up" for MS/MCU. Waist-up cut-outs are placed with `y` > 1 in the beat table.
- **light**: must match the bg it goes on: same direction and colour ("warm torchlight from the right, cool blue moonlight rim from behind").
- **bg space**: say where people will stand ("open stone floor in the lower third, centre clear").
- **Reuse aggressively.** One bg serves several shots. A pose can be reused with `flip`. Target 30–45 images for a short video and 45–70 for a long one.
- **Safety:** never ask for extremist symbols or gore. Infamous real figures appear from behind or in silhouette.

## Round order the user follows
1. Round 1: every `C*_REF`.
2. Round 2: everything else. For each `char` / `full` prompt with `attach`, upload the listed reference image(s) in the same Gemini message.
3. Save each image as `<ID>.png` (jpg/webp also fine) in `06_images/`, then tell Claude.
